Pinczow New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Pińczów, Poland

Demolished. This, Pińczów's newer Jewish cemetery, was established in 1831 about 800 meters southeast of the market square, eventually reaching about 1.5 hectares in an irregular, elongated shape. During WWII, the cemetery was completely destroyed — its fence pulled down and tombstones used for construction — and the Germans carried out executions there, burying victims in mass graves. From the 1960s onward, the area was gradually developed with a school, sports pitch, and single-family houses; after 1980, recovered tombstone fragments were placed in a lapidarium next to the synagogue.
